title: Cap. VI Arg. 3: second Hague reply — God regards faith as medium to life, not condition of election
pass_a_gloss: Secondly they reply, Even if it is not found in so many words in the Scriptures that God elected us with the condition if we believe in him, yet from that it cannot be concluded that God in electing did not have respect to faith. But we rejoin, not only is this not expressed in Scripture in so many words, but not by any equivalent words, nor by any from which it can rightly be deduced. Nor yet do we deny every respect or condition of faith in God electing. For he regards and considers the faith to be ingenerated by himself in the elect, as the medium by which one arrives at life: he does not regard it as a condition antecedently performed or to be performed by men, by means of which one arrives at election itself.
pass_b_english: Second reply: even if Scripture nowhere says in so many words that God elected us on condition we believe, you still cannot conclude he had no regard to faith in electing. We answer: not only is it missing totidem verbis — there are no equivalent words, nothing from which it can rightly be drawn. We do not deny every regard to faith in electing God. He regards the faith he will ingenerate in the elect as the medium by which one reaches life — not as a condition men have already performed or must perform in order to reach election itself.
source_text: Secundo respondent, Etiamsi totidem verbis in Scripturis non reperiatur, Deum nos elegisse cum conditione si in illum credamus, ex eo tamen non posse concludi, Deum in electione non respexisse ad fidem. At regerimus, non modo totidem verbis, sed nullis aequipollentibus, nullis unde id recte deduci potest, hoc exprimi in Scriptura. Neque tamen negamus omnem respectum aut conditionem fidei in Deo eligente. Respicit enim et considerat fidem a se electis ingenerandam, tanquam medium quo pervenitur ad vitam: non respicit tanquam conditionem ab hominibus antecedenter praestitam aut praestandam, qua mediante pervenitur ad ipsam electionem.
